subject: Phased platform-fee amortization, escape clause & support-swap for private deployment
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: platform fee amortization + support tiers for private stack

Hi Monica / Marissa,

Thanks for the last call. Procurement asked for a short note describing three things we need to sign the SOW: (1) whether the platform fee can be amortized across the contract term (we run capex cycles), (2) a clear list of what changes if we pick Gold vs Silver support (oncall windows, response times, escalations), and (3) any "escape" or volume-variance language — our CFO wants a path to reduce the platform fee if actual usage is < 30% of committed baseline after the first 6 months.

Can you put together an approach we can take back to procurement/legal? If there are standard concession guardrails you prefer, share those so we can move quickly.

Appreciate it — Lara
Senior IT Procurement
Acme Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify: platform fee amortization + support tiers for private stack

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Summary below (high level) and I attached a compact price-breakdown and SLA matrix.

Quick answers up front:
- Amortization: Yes — we can amortize the platform fee across the term. Typical structures: (A) 50% upfront, 50% monthly over term; (B) fully monthly amortization with a nominal setup invoiced upfront (recommended for 24+ month deals).
- Support tiers: Silver (business hours, 8x5, 4-hour P1 response), Gold (24x7 oncall, 1-hour P1, named SRE runbook & monthly run-rate reviews).
- Escape / variance: We can include a usage-variance clause after month 6 with a one-time adjustment, subject to a floor and a cap. Typical guardrail: customer may request a platform-fee reduction if sustained usage < 30% of baseline for 60 days; reduction capped at 40% of the platform fee and only available once during the first 12 months. This protects our capacity planning while giving CFO levers.

Proposed next steps:
1) If this approach is acceptable, I will send a tracked-term addendum to legal (cc David) and a revised SOW + DocuSign link.
2) Marissa / Sales: please advise on concession bands (how far we can go on headline discount vs platform-fee amortization).

Attaching: redwood_privdeploy_price_breakdown.xlsx, support_sla_matrix_v2.pdf

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Principal Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme ask — recommended concessioning and legal language

Marissa / David / Ben — quick internal so we have alignment before I go back to Acme. See Lara's note quoted below.

Quoted: "our CFO wants a path to reduce the platform fee if actual usage is < 30% of committed baseline after the first 6 months."

My suggested commercial guardrails (for Sales playbook):
- Offer A (standard): amortize platform fee monthly; require 12-month minimum term; no early reduction other than migration credits.
- Offer B (middle): 50% upfront, 50% amortized monthly over term; allow one usage-variance review after month 6. If usage < 30% for a continuous 60-day window, apply a one-time platform-fee credit equal to 25% of remaining platform-fee liability (minimum floor = 60% of original fee).
- Offer C (concession): same as B but increase one-time credit to 40% in exchange for a 15% non-refundable setup fee and a 12-month reserved capacity commitment.

Legal asks (David): please see suggested language below for the escape clause: 
"If Customer demonstrates sustained usage below thirty percent (30%) of the Baseline for a continuous sixty (60) day period after the sixth (6th) month, Customer may request a one-time adjustment to the Platform Fee. Any such adjustment shall be no greater than forty percent (40%) of the remaining Platform Fee and shall not reduce Customer's Platform Fee liability below sixty percent (60%) of the originally invoiced Platform Fee. Customer must provide written notice and data evidencing usage; Redwood will have thirty (30) days to validate."

Ben: what concessions on the list price and up-front discount are safe here if we offer Offer B? My thought: up to 12% headline discount in exchange for Offer B mechanics (amortized + one-time review). Anything more and we push to Offer C.

I plan to send a clean term addendum + SOW tomorrow once we align.

Thanks — M

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:01:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Internal: Acme ask — recommended concessioning and legal language

All — agree with Monica's triaged offers. A few practical notes from Sales playbook and previous deals: 
- Concession bands: up to 12% net discount with Offer B is acceptable for deal size ~USD 1.2M ARR equivalent; push beyond that and require Exec sign-off.
- Amortization ops: Finance prefers 50% upfront for deals < 18 months; for >=24 months fully monthly amortization is fine.
- Escape validation: require Acme to ship token-level billing report (we'll provide schema) and allow Redwood a one-time audit during the 30-day validation window.
- Support-swap practical: Gold includes quarterly runbooks and a named SRE; Silver does not include oncall burn downs. If they pick Gold we can remove a 10% engineering holdback often included for pilot projects.

I recommend we present Offer B as our standard middle path in the commercial email — it's a balance and keeps us protected while being procurement-friendly.

I'll review the addendum language once David posts his redlines.

-Marissa
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Subject: RE: Clarify: platform fee amortization + support tiers for private stack — proposed commercial terms

Hi Lara / Acme team — following our internal alignment, attached is a concise commercial addendum and a redlined SOW that implements the Offer B mechanics we discussed. High level: 

- Platform fee amortization: 50% upfront, 50% amortized monthly over the 24-month term (invoiced monthly).
- Usage-variance escape: Customer may request a one-time adjustment after month 6 if sustained usage < 30% of Baseline for 60 continuous days. Adjustment capped at 40% of remaining Platform Fee liability and not to reduce liability below 60% of the originally invoiced Platform Fee. Process: written notice + token-level report + 30-day validation window.
- Support tiers: see attached support_sla_matrix_v2.pdf — Silver = 8x5 business-hour support; Gold = 24x7 on-call with 1-hour P1 response, named SRE, monthly operational review.
- Commercial trade: Offer B includes a 10% headline discount on list for this SOW; Offer C (if you prefer a larger headline concession) would trade a 15% non-refundable setup fee and 15% discount for a guaranteed reserved capacity commitment.

Attachments: SOW_vpc_starter_v1.pdf (SOW), redwood_privdeploy_price_breakdown.xlsx (breakdown), support_sla_matrix_v2.pdf

If this works, we can send a DocuSign package this afternoon: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-PRV-2026-0701

Please let me know any quick redlines. If you want to loop legal (Jordan) into a short call, happy to schedule.

Best,
